html:
An oasis city in the Tafilalt valley of southern Morocco, founded in 757 on the edge of the Sahara. For six centuries it was the northern port of the trans-Saharan trade, where caravans set out for the gold lands of West Africa.

Caravans carried salt, cloth, copper and horses south across the desert and came back with gold from Ghana and later the Mali Empire. Sijilmasa's mint turned the gold into dinars, and its merchants were famed for their wealth; a 10th century traveller wrote of a credit note worth 42,000 dinars. It was founded by Berbers of the Miknasa tribe, and in 909 the future first Fatimid caliph was held prisoner there before his rise.

The Almoravids took the city in 1055 at the start of their conquests. In 1352 Ibn Battuta set out from Sijilmasa on his journey to Mali. The city declined in the 14th and 15th centuries as trade shifted to other routes, and only ruins remain near the town of Rissani.
